headline: $406M in long liquidations and Brent back at $106 push BTC below its value area; ETFs bled $681M last week as the market waits for Wednesday's CPI.
summary: The market stage stays bull (since 10/09; 33 straight closes above a rising 200-day average), and no exit-framework rule is triggered or close. Monday's drop was a leverage flush plus macro pressure from oil and yields: funding cooled and risk reversals tilted to puts, but valuation and on-chain structure did not change. Next to watch: Monday's ETF flows (published 10/13), US September CPI on 10/14 at 12:30 UTC (20:30 Taipei), and the 80,000 and 76–78K supply zones.

news.title: BTC broke below 82,000 Monday evening; $489M liquidated market-wide in 24 hours, $406M of it longs (83.2%), $107M in BTC positions
news.read: A leverage flush: Deribit funding on this site fell from 8.08% to 6.28%, Hyperliquid turned negative at −3.97%, and the 30-day risk reversal at −2.42 shows more demand for protection. Funding and chase-long positioning had risen in the prior edition and were washed out today. Deribit perpetual open interest is still only about $858M, so this is not a large-scale deleveraging; it is short-term noise that does not change the market stage, and the 200-day average is still 11.9% below.

news.title: Houthis attack Saudi Arabia and two tankers are hit near Hormuz; Brent rises 2% Monday to $106.80, a two-week high. Zelensky accuses Russia of breaking the energy ceasefire the same day
news.read: The prior edition's 'energy ceasefire' tailwind was erased within a day. Higher oil lifts inflation expectations, in the same direction as this site's high-rate backdrop (10-year 5.22%, real yield 2.87%), and is one macro reason for the ETF outflows. If oil stays above $100 it will weigh on CPI and rate-cut hopes; that affects flows, but it is not an exit-framework condition.

news.title: US September CPI out Wednesday: headline seen +0.5–0.6% m/m and about 3.6% y/y, core about +0.19% m/m; CME FedWatch puts a 25 bp hike on 10/28 at 19.4% (42.5% a month ago)
news.read: Energy lifting headline CPI is consensus; core is what matters. Core ≥ 0.3% could revive October hike bets, ≤ 0.2% favors a Fed hold. With a 0.682 30-day BTC–Nasdaq correlation, CPI will move BTC short term through yields and equities, but it will not change the market stage (set by the 200-day average) or on-chain valuation.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs saw about $681M of net outflows over 10/05–10/09; Friday 10/09 had a small $21.13M net inflow (SoSoValue)
news.read: Consistent with this site: 10/07 −$487.1M, 10/08 −$244.1M (The Block), 10/09 provisional +$21.1M. Glassnode's weekly also attributes this week's pullback to selling by perp traders and ETF holders. ETFs are the largest marginal buyer this cycle; continued outflows would make the 1.27M BTC of underwater supply at 84–86K harder to absorb, but realized cap is still +1.27% over 30 days, so capital has not turned to net outflow.

news.title: Strategy bought 250 BTC over 10/05–10/11 ($21.5M, average 86,194), bringing holdings to 848,250 BTC; it also repurchased $192M of STRC preferred stock
news.read: A fourth straight week of buying, but only about one-ninth the size of the buyback, so its BTC buying stays weak; its USD cash reserve fell to about $5.5B. Against last week's −$681M ETF outflow, corporate buying cannot offset it. For reference only; it changes no framework condition.

news.title: South Korea's Jeonbuk Bank issues the first won-denominated corporate loan collateralized by BTC; on default the collateral is auctioned through the courts under civil-enforcement rules effective 10/01
news.read: A traditional bank accepting BTC as collateral is a long-term adoption step, but the amount, rate and loan-to-value are undisclosed, so there is no quantifiable near-term demand effect. None of this site's indicators change; background only.

news.title: SWI Group raises €800M (about $894M) to convert the US and Swedish sites of former FTX-backed miner Genesis Digital to AI compute and sell its Kazakhstan sites
news.read: Miners pivoting to AI is an ongoing industry trend that could pull some hashrate offline over time, but hashrate here is 1,021.6 EH/s (7-day mean), up 6.26% on the week, and the 30/60-day hash ribbons show no capitulation, so no near-term effect is visible.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 42
items.points: Thursday's break below 81K returned price to where the breakout began three weeks ago; the week closed about 3% lower. Weekly ETF net flow +$118M → −$702M; perp CVD fell to −$682M; 25Δ skew 2.1% → 4.46%; supply in profit 74.5% → 71.4%; monthly realized cap change +1.2%.
items.meaning: Consistent with this site: risk reversal −2.42, ETF outflows, realized cap still growing. Its weekly ETF figure uses a different basis from this site's −$681M, so the two are not netted. Short-term structure; it does not change the market stage or exit framework.

items.title: The Week On-chain: A Rally Running Light
items.points: Sell wall at 86.5K–86.75K, largest bid wall 81K–81.25K; reclaiming 85.5K is needed for recovery. New capital over 30 days about $4.9B vs a $12.8B realized cap increase; long liquidation band 81.7K–83.3K, then 75K.
items.meaning: The 10/12 close at 81,737 has cut through its 81.7K–83.3K long liquidation band, matching Monday's $406M of long liquidations; the close is still near the 81K bid wall. The next reference level, 75K, is close to this site's 76–78K supply zone.
